name: Thymoma Type B

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Thymic Epithelial Tumors

criteria.description: Histological identification of epithelial cells with lymphocyte-rich background consistent with WHO type B thymoma
Presence of anterior mediastinal mass on CT or MRI consistent with thymoma
Positive staining for cytokeratin and CD5 with characteristic lymphocyte markers
Symptoms or signs related to mass effect or paraneoplastic syndromes such as myasthenia gravis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of type B thymoma with supportive imaging and immunohistochemical findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histology, imaging, and immunohistochemistry per WHO guidelines

pathognomonic.symptomName: Anterior mediastinal mass detected on imaging
searchTerms: mass in front of chest detected by scan

pathognomonic.symptomName: Myasthenia gravis with fluctuating skeletal muscle weakness
pathognomonic.notes: Common paraneoplastic syndrome associated with thymoma type B
searchTerms: weakness in skeletal muscles varying over time

common.symptomName: Dyspnea due to mass effect on respiratory structures
common.notes: Compression of airways or lung tissue
searchTerms: breathing difficulty from pressure on lungs
dyspnea caused by mass effect on respiratory tract
shortness of breath due to airway compression

common.symptomName: Chest pain localized to anterior mediastinum
common.notes: Due to tumor invasion or compression
searchTerms: chest pain in front of chest
symptoms from blocked superior vena cava
swelling and breathing issues from vein obstruction
signs of superior vena cava blockage

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement
searchTerms: hoarse voice due to nerve involvement

occasional.symptomName: Weight loss unrelated to other causes
searchTerms: weight loss not caused by diet or illness
anemia from red blood cell production failure
pure red cell aplasia related to cancer
low red blood cells due to bone marrow suppression

rare.symptomName: Superior phrenic nerve palsy causing diaphragmatic paralysis
searchTerms: phrenic nerve damage leading to breathing problems

rare.symptomName: Pericardial effusion secondary to tumor invasion
searchTerms: fluid around heart from tumor invasion
pericardial fluid buildup caused by cancer
heart sac effusion secondary to tumor
brain inflammation causing memory and mood changes

laboratory: Elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies in myasthenia gravis
Anemia in pure red cell aplasia
Normal routine blood counts unless paraneoplastic syndromes present
imaging: CT scan showing well-defined anterior mediastinal mass
MRI to assess local invasion and vascular involvement
PET scan may show variable FDG uptake
genetic: Somatic mutations in GTF2I gene reported in some type B thymomas
other: Histopathology demonstrating epithelial cells with abundant lymphocytes
Immunohistochemistry positive for cytokeratin and CD5

distinguishingFeatures: More aggressive histology with cytologic atypia
Higher rate of local invasion and metastasis
Diffuse lymphoid proliferation without epithelial component

redFlags: Signs of superior vena cava syndrome
references: Travis WD, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Lung, Pleura, Thymus and Heart. IARC; 2015.
